mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past three months signals an active monetary easing cycle, reducing discount rates on future corporate earnings and increasing equity valuations, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in periods where FEDFUNDS declines, as measured by a t-test p-value > 0.05, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate above 9.5% over a 3-month window signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which triggers a flight to safety and reduces equity risk appetite, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 9.5% for three consecutive months, or the signal fails to outperform a random baseline in walk-forward testing.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both residential construction (HOUST) and real personal consumption (RSAFS) indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS fails to predict negative 60-day SPX returns, with Rank IC < 0.03 or t-test p-value > 0.05 in walk-forward analysis.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in industrial production (INDPRO) below 95.0 for two consecutive months signals a contraction in real output, which increases recession risk and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during INDPRO < 95.0 periods, as confirmed by t-test p > 0.05 or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.0% and CPIAUCSL is above 214.0, it indicates a high-inflation, tight-money regime where real rates are elevated, reducing equity attractiveness and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition of FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and CPIAUCSL > 214.0 fails to predict negative 5-day SPX returns, with Rank IC < 0.03 or t-test p > 0.05 in walk-forward testing.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in residential construction (HOUST) above 580.0 after two consecutive months below 570.0 signals a recovery in housing demand, which boosts confidence in the broader economy and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive following HOUST rebounds from below 570.0, as confirmed by t-test p > 0.05 or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in non-farm payroll growth (PAYEMS) above 200k in a single month, combined with a declining unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals strong labor market tightening, which increases inflation expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 200k AND UNRATE declines > 0.2pp in one month
failure_condition: The joint signal of PAYEMS > 200k and UNRATE decline > 0.2pp fails to predict negative 60-day SPX returns, with Rank IC < 0.03 or t-test p > 0.05 in walk-forward analysis.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption (RSAFS) below 350,000 million dollars for two consecutive months, combined with a contraction in GDP (GDPC1) below 12,800 billion, indicates a deepening demand slump, which triggers negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition of RSAFS < 350000 and GDPC1 < 12800 fails to predict negative 60-day SPX returns, with Rank IC < 0.03 or t-test p > 0.05 in walk-forward testing.
